<reason>B more convincingly distinguished protecting public access from punishing sheltering itself, while directly answering questions about accessibility assessments and obstructed playgrounds. A established genuine benefits from clearing particular locations, but did not adequately weigh displaced hazards and disrupted support or resolve successive removals with nowhere lawful to go. Its repeated preference-veto objection also failed to engage B’s explicit distinction between objective inability and mere dislike.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B answered A’s reoccupation challenge by explaining that sweeps also cannot guarantee against return, while safety and access requirements can be enforced against recurrence. A largely repeated its prevention objection without establishing why those narrower powers were insufficient.</best_rebuttal>
